title: Continuity and Change in a Community Library: A Lecture Analysis
instructions: 阅读一篇关于社区图书馆制度延续与变革的讲座分析文章（约800–1100词）。先阅读文章，然后完成10道题（单选、填空、匹配/标题、判断正误/未提及）。题目中的英文提示简短，答案必须基于原文。之后学习语法点“指代、词性与平行结构；长句拆解”，并完成8道新句子的语法题。最后进行口语和写作迁移练习。所有场景和数据均为模拟教育材料，不是官方雅思考试，也不代表任何分数。
passage:
Good morning, everyone. Today I want to analyse how institutions balance continuity and change, using the example of a small community library called the Riverside Library. This is a simulated case study for our discussion, not a real institution. I will look at three periods: its founding in 1985, its crisis in 2008, and its renewal in 2020. My aim is to show that continuity and change are not opposites; they often depend on each other. In fact, the ability to adapt while preserving core values is what allows institutions to survive over time.

A. Founding and Early Stability (1985–2000)

The Riverside Library opened in 1985 in a converted warehouse. Its founders, a group of local teachers, wanted to provide free books and a quiet study space for adults who had left school early. The library was run by a volunteer committee of seven members. The committee met once a month and made all decisions by consensus. Funding came from small donations and a yearly book sale. The library had no paid staff until 1995, when it hired its first part-time librarian. Even then, the volunteer committee kept control of the budget. This structure remained unchanged for fifteen years. Members of the community trusted the library because it was clearly run by people like themselves. The library’s collection grew slowly but steadily, from 1,200 books in 1985 to 5,000 in 2000. The building was old, but the library was a stable and familiar place. This stability was not passive; it was actively maintained through regular meetings and shared decision-making, which built a strong sense of ownership among local residents.

B. Crisis and Adaptation (2008–2015)

In 2008, the library faced a serious crisis. The local council cut its small annual grant, and donations fell during a national economic downturn. The volunteer committee realised that the old model could not continue. They held a public meeting and proposed three changes. First, they introduced a paid director to manage daily operations. Second, they started charging a small membership fee for borrowing new books, while keeping older books free. Third, they began offering evening classes in computer skills and English conversation. These changes were controversial. Some long-time volunteers felt that the library was becoming too commercial. However, the paid director, a woman named Sarah Chen, argued that the library needed a stable income to survive. She also pointed out that the evening classes attracted new users, especially young adults. By 2012, membership had increased by 40 percent, and the library was financially stable again. The volunteer committee still existed, but its role changed: it now advised the director rather than making all decisions. This shift from full control to an advisory role was difficult for some members, but most accepted it because the library survived. The crisis forced the library to rethink its operations, but it did so without abandoning its commitment to free access for older materials and community involvement.

C. Renewal and New Continuity (2020–present)

In 2020, the library faced a different challenge: the COVID-19 pandemic. The building closed for six months, but the library did not stop working. The director and volunteers quickly created an online borrowing system and a delivery service for elderly members. They also started a weekly online reading group. These new services were popular, and many members asked to keep them after the building reopened. The library then made a second set of changes. It hired a part-time digital coordinator, expanded its online collection, and began offering hybrid events that people could attend in person or online. At the same time, the library kept its original mission: free access to books and a quiet space for study. The volunteer committee, now called the Community Advisory Board, still meets monthly and still makes recommendations. The library’s collection has grown to 12,000 books, and it now serves about 2,500 members. What is interesting is that the library’s core values—free access, community control, and a quiet space—have remained stable, even as its methods have changed dramatically. The library changed its structure to preserve its purpose. That is the paradox of institutional continuity: sometimes you must change in order to stay the same. The pandemic accelerated digital transformation, but it also reinforced the library’s role as a community hub, proving that physical and virtual services can complement each other.

In conclusion, the Riverside Library shows that continuity and change are not a simple choice between old and new. The library survived because its leaders were willing to adapt its structures while protecting its core mission. The volunteer committee lost some power but gained a new role. The paid director brought stability but had to respect the community’s values. The online services expanded access but did not replace the physical space. For anyone studying institutions, the lesson is clear: successful institutions do not resist change; they manage it carefully, always asking what must be preserved and what can be adapted. By balancing tradition with innovation, they ensure that their fundamental purpose endures even as the world around them evolves.

grammar.title: 指代、词性与平行结构；长句拆解
grammar.explanation: 在英语长句中，代词（it, they, this, these）常指代前文的名词或整个句子，理解指代是拆解长句的第一步。其次，注意词性：同一个词根可能以名词、动词、形容词形式出现，例如 decide (动词) → decision (名词) → decisive (形容词)。平行结构要求并列成分词性一致、形式对称，例如 “to provide free books and a quiet study space” 中 provide 后接两个名词短语。拆解长句时，先找主句的主语和谓语，再处理从句和修饰成分。本课新讲“指代与平行结构在长句中的配合”，复习“词性转换”。
grammar.example: The library changed its structure to preserve its purpose.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct pronoun: The volunteers held a meeting because ______ wanted to discuss the budget.
questions.explanation: 主语 The volunteers 是复数，指代人，因此用 they。
questions.evidence: The volunteers held a meeting because they wanted to discuss the budget.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word form: The committee made a ______ to hire a director.
questions.explanation: 冠词 a 后需要名词，decision 是名词形式。
questions.evidence: The committee made a decision to hire a director.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct parallel structure: The library offers free books, quiet spaces, and ______.
questions.explanation: 并列成分 free books, quiet spaces 都是名词短语，因此第三个也应是名词短语 evening classes。
questions.evidence: The library offers free books, quiet spaces, and evening classes.

questions.prompt: What does “it” refer to? The director expanded the online collection because it attracted new users.
questions.explanation: 从句主语 it 指代前文提到的 the online collection，因为吸引新用户的是在线馆藏。
questions.evidence: The director expanded the online collection because it attracted new users.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word form: The library’s ______ depends on stable funding.
questions.explanation: 所有格 the library’s 后需要名词，survival 是名词。
questions.evidence: The library’s survival depends on stable funding.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct parallel structure: The volunteers wanted to protect the mission and ______ the building.
questions.explanation: wanted to protect 与 wanted to maintain 并列，to 后接动词原形，因此用 maintain。
questions.evidence: The volunteers wanted to protect the mission and maintain the building.

questions.prompt: What does “this” refer to? The library started charging a small fee. This helped it survive.
questions.explanation: this 指代前一句整个动作“开始收取小额费用”，该动作帮助图书馆生存。
questions.evidence: The library started charging a small fee. This helped it survive.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word form: The new services were very ______ with members.
questions.explanation: 系动词 were 后需要形容词作表语，popular 是形容词。
questions.evidence: The new services were very popular with members.
